column5: UConn Greenhouse IPM (Pundt, 2011, revised 2024) read in full: the six programme components, prevention before a crop (pet plants, weeds, algae, debris under benches), cultural links (nitrogen and pests, salts and Pythium, overwatering), sanitation list, scouting tools, yellow sticky cards at a minimum of one per 1,000 square feet with extras by doors and vents, five to ten random sites per 4,000 square feet in an M or zigzag, indicator plants, and weekly grower-scout review all match module 6.

UConn IPM extra scouting points: inspect roots as well as leaves and stems, since healthy roots are white and actively growing and decay or fungus gnat feeding shows there; check the middle of benches (less spray coverage) and bench ends (less air movement), hanging baskets and floor crops; discard heavily infested plants in bins with tight lids so winged pests cannot fly back; biological controls work best alongside good cultural control and consistent monitoring.

UConn IPM's pesticide record lists the product's EPA registration number, a US identifier. For a UK greenhouse the equivalent identifier on an authorised product label is the MAPP number; the record should also hold product, amount, area, crop, date and location, and for biocontrol the number, type and place of release.
